claims.text: Every Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime session is stateful and runs in its own Firecracker microVM with a dedicated filesystem and shell, so one user's session cannot bleed into another's.
AgentCore Runtime assumes an IAM role the customer controls, can require JWTs from the customer's identity provider on inbound requests, and can reach private resources through VPC networking.
AgentCore Gateway can apply Cedar policies that gate a tool call by who is asking, which tool, under what condition, and with which arguments.

For SaaS tokens, AgentCore can run the three-legged OAuth flow, store the result in an encrypted Token Vault bound to a specific user-and-agent pair, and inject it into the outbound call so the raw secret never enters the prompt or model context.

AgentCore treats invocation input as trusted and does not sanitize input, filter content blocks, or enforce behavioral limits, so validation of untrusted users' input is the customer's responsibility.
AgentCore Identity assigns unique, verifiable identities to agents, enabling fine-grained access control and secure interactions with enterprise systems.
AgentCore Gateway converts APIs, Lambda functions, and existing services into Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible tools that agents can discover through a single secure endpoint.
AgentCore Memory is a managed memory system that maintains both immediate (short-term) and long-term knowledge so agents can retain context across interactions.

AgentCore Runtime is a secure, serverless environment for hosting agents and tools, compatible with CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and Strands Agents and with any foundation model inside or outside Bedrock.
AgentCore Observability provides tracing, real-time dashboards and standardized telemetry that visualize an agent's entire execution path for debugging and auditing.

The AgentCore harness, generally available since 17 June 2026, lets users declare the model, tools, skills and instructions while AgentCore handles environment, compute, memory, identity, networking and observability; AWS recommends it in place of Bedrock Agents Classic.
AWS's own comparison says routing-mode multi-agent is "not straightforward today" on the AgentCore harness and that full multi-agent collaboration "requires custom framework code".
LangGraph uses a graph of nodes and edges, with checkpointers keyed by thread_id and interrupts for approval.
LangGraph is documented as hostable on Foundry hosted agents and AgentCore Runtime.

LangGraph is a low-level orchestration runtime where shared state determines what each node reads, writes and does next; conditional edges handle branches and human-in-the-loop interrupts can pause the graph until a person approves or modifies the next action.
With LangGraph, the team must still design state schemas, reducers, retry behavior, tool contracts and termination conditions.

Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 shipped for .NET and Python on 3 April 2026; it supports graph workflows plus sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat and Magentic patterns, with checkpointing, pause and resume.
Microsoft Agent Framework's Durable Extension was in preview at 1.0 and enables hosting on Azure Functions; Foundry hosted agents also host it.

Microsoft Agent Framework combines AutoGen's conversational multi-agent abstractions with Semantic Kernel's session-based state management, middleware, telemetry and type safety, and adds graph-based workflows with type-safe routing.
Microsoft Agent Framework emits OpenTelemetry GenAI spans for agent, model and tool calls, with sensitive data off by default; the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions were still in Development status.
When deployed through Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Agent Framework agents can opt into task-adherence guardrails, PII protection and prompt-injection defenses.
CrewAI provides Crews (role-based agents running tasks sequentially, via a hierarchical manager, or a hybrid) and Flows (stateful workflows with events, routers and steps).
CrewAI Flows have built-in persistence via `@persist`, backed by SQLite by default.
CrewAI is documented as hostable on AgentCore Runtime, and CrewAI AMP offers managed deployment and a no-code studio.

The OpenAI Agents SDK provides agents, handoffs, agents as tools, guardrails, sessions, human in the loop and sandbox agents; it was still on 0.x releases (Python 0.24.0 on 15 Oct 2026) and is paired with Temporal for durability in long runs.
